name: John (Elivin \ Elwin) 1st Minister of Southold Long Island Yonges \ Younges of Brynyorken \ Youngs Rev.
bioAdditions: Youngs Family (1907) prints the inscription on Rev. John Youngs's altar tomb: 'Mr Iohn Yongs Minister of the Word and First Setler of the Chvrch of Christ in Sovth Hovld ... Deceased the 24 of Febrvary ... 1671/2 and of His Age 74' (S1). It gives his marriages as (1) Joan Herrington at Southwold, 25 July 1622 (license of 24 July 1622, bond by Mr. Christopher Yongs), (2) Joan (Harris), widow of Richard Palgrave, and (3) Mary (Warren), widow Gardner, who died at Southold in 1678. His children were John, Thomas, Mary (m. Edward Petty), Rachel, Joseph, Benjamin and Christopher. No daughter married William Wells (S1). The deed of gift of Mary Mapes (formerly Wells), 1678, shows that the Youngs link to the Wells family came through Mary Wells's daughter Mary, who married a John Youngs (S2). He is therefore not an ancestor on present evidence.

confidenceRecommendation.justification: Downgrade in substance: not an ancestor on present evidence. Youngs 1907 lists no Mary who married William Wells, and the 1678 Mapes deed explains the Youngs tradition. Mark as not ancestral, or remove.

sources.citation: Selah Youngs Jr., Youngs Family: Vicar Christopher Yonges, his ancestors in England and his descendants in America (1907), pp. 38-41 (First and Second Generations)
sources.supports: tomb inscription, marriages and children of Rev. John

sources.citation: J. Wickham Case, ed., Southold Town Records, vol. 1 (1882), pp. 302-303: deed of gift 26 Dec 1678 (recorded 3 Apr 1679) by 'Mary Mapes of Southold ... the relect of William Wells of ye sd Town ... lately desceased, and now wife to Thomas Mapes Junr', who had received all Wells's lands and goods by his deed of gift, to 'my son in law John Yongs, in right of his wife and to Mary Yongs his wife my daughter' (witnesses Thomas Mapes, William Wells); also an entry (Liber page 141, 1677) of meadow had 'of Mary Mapes formerly ye wife of Mr William Wells, in part of pay for teaching her son William his tread'
sources.supports: Youngs connection via the daughter Mary (Wells) Youngs

researchLogEntry: Round 4: Youngs 1907 and the 1678 Mapes deed confirm Rev. John Youngs is not William Wells's father-in-law.
